validated_results.title: Urinary melatonin levels, sleep disruption, and risk of prostate cancer in elderly men.
validated_results.reason: Prospective case-cohort study evaluating urinary melatonin metabolite levels and risk of incident prostate cancer.

sample_size.excerpt: We undertook a case–cohort study of 928 Icelandic men without prostate cancer (PCa) nested within the Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility (AGES)-Reykjavik cohort to investigate the prospective association between first morning-void urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (6-STM) levels and the subsequent risk for PCa, under the hypothesis that men with lower 6-STM levels have an increased risk for advanced PCa.

cases.excerpt: A total of 111 men were diagnosed with incident PCa, including 24 with advanced disease.

comparison.excerpt: 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (6-STM) levels were dichotomized at the median in subcohort (17.14 ng/ml); HR compares low 6- STM levels (below the median) to high levels (above the median).

design.excerpt: We undertook a case–cohort study ( Supplemental Fig. 1 ) within the Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibililty-Reykjavik (AGES-Reykjavik) study

timing.excerpt: investigate the prospective association between first morning-void urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (6-STM) levels and the subsequent risk for PCa

continent.excerpt: We undertook a case–cohort study of 928 Icelandic men without prostate cancer (PCa) nested within the Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility (AGES)-Reykjavik cohort

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Subjects collected a first morning-void urine sample. Urine samples were assayed for 6-STM using the melatonin-sulfate enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (IBL International, Toronto, ON, Canada).
